newsitem.title: UK: Birmingham City brings AIM total to over 1 bln stg.
newsitem.headline: Birmingham City brings AIM total to over 1 bln stg.

text.p: Soccer club Birmingham City's debut on the London Stock Exchange's Alternative Investment Market (AIM) on Friday brought the total raised by companies on AIM to just over 1.0 billion pounds ($1.6 billion), the Stock Exchange said.
By 1100 GMT, Birmingam City's shares were quoted at 57-1/2p, setting a premium on their 50p placing price, although no trade was registered in the stock.

The football club, the latest in a series to float on the UK stock market, raised 7.5 million pounds and valued the club at 25.0 million. The proceeds will go to improve the club's ground and increase working capital, the club said.
Over 260 companies are traded on AIM, the London Stock Exchange's market for smaller, young and fast-growing companies, and the market is worth nearly 6.0 billion stg, the Exchange said.

"AIM has proved to be a very valuable source of funding for small and growing companies," the Exchange said. "We continue to work with market participants to help companies understand the advantages of joining a public market." ($ = 0.623 British Pounds)
